reasoning: The leaf shows numerous very small (1-3mm) reddish-brown to dark necrotic specks scattered across the surface of an otherwise green tomato leaf. This pattern — tiny discrete spots without concentric rings, large necrotic zones, or powdery coating — is the classic presentation of bacterial speck caused by Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato. Septoria is possible but typically produces slightly larger spots with tan centers; the spots here are too small and uniformly dark for Septoria.
